**Visa and Mastercard join agentic payments alliance with over 25 founding members**

*A new cross-industry body to set standards for AI-initiated commerce marks the clearest signal yet that card networks view agentic payments as an infrastructure category, not a research project.*

More than 25 companies have launched the Agentic Payments Alliance (APA), a coalition aimed at guiding the development of commerce initiated by AI agents. Founding members include Visa, Mastercard, Fiserv, Circle, Solana and Remitly, among others. The group's formation follows a run of individual agentic payments announcements from its members over the past six months, from Visa's partnership with OpenAI to Mastercard's work with ING and Worldline on Europe's first agentic transaction.

Moving from bilateral pilots to a multi-stakeholder body suggests the industry recognises that agentic commerce will require shared protocols for authentication, liability and settlement rather than proprietary schemes. That both major card networks are founding members, alongside a stablecoin issuer and a blockchain platform, signals the alliance intends to be rail-agnostic rather than card-centric.

For European payments firms, the APA's composition is worth watching. The inclusion of Circle and Solana alongside the card networks points to an assumption that agentic payments will span both traditional and token-based rails. Whether the alliance produces binding standards or remains a talking shop will depend on whether it attracts banks and regulators as participants.

*Sources: [Visa and Mastercard back new Agentic Payments Alliance](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48265/visa-and-mastercard-back-new-agentic-payments-alliance?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Banca d'Italia finds stablecoins offer no cost or speed edge for remittances**

*Research from Italy's central bank challenges the narrative that stablecoins can undercut traditional remittance channels, with implications for MiCA-era business models and the digital euro debate.*

Researchers at Banca d'Italia have concluded that stablecoins show no systematic cost advantage over traditional remittance channels for cross-border payments. The finding, published on August 19, directly challenges one of the most commonly cited use cases for regulated stablecoins under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

The research arrives as several European stablecoin ventures position themselves for cross-border payments, including the Visa- and Mastercard-backed Open USD launched on July 1 and AllUnity's Swedish krona stablecoin announced earlier this year. If the cost and speed claims that underpin these business cases do not hold up under central bank scrutiny, the commercial logic for stablecoin remittance corridors narrows considerably.

The timing also feeds into the digital euro debate. The European Central Bank has framed the digital euro partly as a response to private stablecoin growth. If stablecoins prove less disruptive to existing payment flows than assumed, it could shift the policy rationale for a central bank digital currency toward sovereignty arguments rather than competitive necessity.

*Sources: [Stablecoins offer little cost or speed advantage for remittances - Banca d'Italia](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48266/stablecoins-offer-little-cost-or-speed-advantage-for-remittances---banca-ditalia?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**PSR publishes annual report covering fraud reimbursement and market oversight**

*The Payment Systems Regulator's 2025-26 annual report provides its first full-year assessment since mandatory APP fraud reimbursement took effect, alongside updates on its card scheme market review.*

The Payment Systems Regulator (PSR) published its annual report and accounts for 2025-26 on August 17. The report covers the regulator's first full operating year since mandatory authorised push payment fraud reimbursement came into force, and follows its July finding that the regime cut APP fraud losses by £73 million in its initial period.

The annual report also covers the PSR's ongoing market review of card scheme fees, which in the first half of 2025 led to a proposal requiring Visa and Mastercard to report UK profit figures. That work continues alongside the broader UK government consultation on modernising payments regulation, which opened in July and could reshape the PSR's own mandate.

The report, covering a full year of regulatory activity across fraud, competition and open banking, provides a useful benchmark for industry participants tracking UK regulatory direction.

*Sources: [PSR Annual Report and Accounts 2025-26](https://www.regulationtomorrow.com/2026/08/psr-annual-report-and-accounts-2025-26/) — Global Regulation Tomorrow*

**UK mobile wallet registrations reach 57% of adults**

*Fresh industry data shows mobile wallets are gaining ground against physical cards in the UK, though card payments still dominate overall volumes.*

Mobile wallets are reshaping where consumer loyalty sits in UK payments, with 57% of adults now registered with at least one provider, according to the latest industry data reported by Finextra. Cards continue to dominate UK payment volumes, but mobile wallet adoption is accelerating as contactless NFC payments become routine at the point of sale.

The figures sharpen the competitive challenge facing pay-by-bank services. As mobile wallets become the default interface for card payments, account-to-account alternatives must compete not just on cost but on the convenience of a wallet experience that consumers already use daily. The UK Payments Initiative and commercial variable recurring payments face the same challenge: matching an embedded user experience that more than half the adult population already relies on.

For card networks, the wallet layer, rather than the plastic card, is increasingly where consumer attachment forms. That makes partnerships with Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay as strategically important as the underlying scheme relationships with issuing banks.

*Sources: [Mobile wallets gain traction in the UK](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48268/mobile-wallets-gain-traction-in-the-uk?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**PPRO partners with Blik to develop agentic commerce for Polish payments**

*The partnership extends the agentic payments trend into central Europe's largest domestic payment scheme, connecting Blik's 35 million users to emerging AI-initiated commerce flows.*

PPRO is partnering with Blik to develop agentic commerce capabilities for local payments in Poland. The collaboration aims to connect Blik, which dominates Polish digital payments, with the emerging ecosystem of AI agent-initiated transactions.

Poland's payments market is distinctive in Europe for the dominance of a single domestic scheme. Blik processed over three billion transactions in 2025 and is embedded in virtually every Polish banking app. Connecting this infrastructure to agentic commerce flows could give Poland an early-mover position in a part of Europe where card network alternatives already have less grip.

The deal follows a pattern of European domestic schemes positioning for agentic payments. Wero, Blik and iDEAL have all taken steps to ensure they are not bypassed as AI-initiated commerce develops. For payment orchestrators like PPRO, these partnerships are a way to ensure their merchant clients can accept agentic transactions across fragmented European payment methods.

*Sources: [PPRO partners with Blik to enable agentic commerce for local payments in Poland](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110669/ppro-partners-with-blik-to-enable-agentic-commerce-for-local-payments-in-poland?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*
